scope: Research for Pilot 3 (Ugin's Allies and Heroes): Ugin's documented alliances and encounters in official Wizards story pages. Targeted, not exhaustive. No decklist is proposed here.

tdm_ep6.title: Tarkir: Dragonstorm | Episode 6: How Wretched Love

claims.subject: ugin

evidence.quote: Long ago, the world-devouring Eldrazi were sealed away on Zendikar by three Planeswalkers: the spirit dragon Ugin; the vampire Sorin Markov; and a third Planeswalker called the Lithomancer
three Planeswalkers collaborated to trap the monstrous Eldrazi on the world of Zendikar

claims.summary: Ugin, Sorin and Nahiri together imprisoned the Eldrazi titans on Zendikar.
claims.limitation: Stone and Blood dates this to six thousand years before Eldritch Moon; this pack records no AR year.

claims.subject: nahiri

evidence.quote: the underground chamber that she and Sorin had named the Eye of Ugin

claims.summary: Nahiri and Sorin named the chamber at the centre of the prison the Eye of Ugin.

claims.subject: nahiri

evidence.quote: Nahiri, a kor of Zendikar, stood vigil over the prisoners.

claims.summary: Nahiri stayed on Zendikar as the Eldrazi prison's warden.

claims.subject: ugin

evidence.quote: Ugin, called the Spirit Dragon, and the vampire Sorin Markov agreed to return if their aid was needed.

claims.summary: Ugin and Sorin agreed to come back if the prison needed them.

claims.subject: ugin

evidence.quote: But the Eldrazi nearly escaped over a thousand years ago, and neither Sorin nor Ugin came.

claims.summary: When the Eldrazi nearly escaped, neither Ugin nor Sorin answered, leaving Nahiri to contain them alone.
claims.limitation: The reasons for Ugin's absence are not stated in this source.

claims.subject: sorin_markov

evidence.quote: Sorin has found his way here, to Ugin's home world, in search of his old ally.
Sorin has found his way here, to Ugin's home world, in search of his old ally.

claims.summary: After the Eldrazi escaped, Sorin came to Tarkir looking for Ugin.

claims.subject: sorin_markov

evidence.quote: In another timeline, Sorin found Ugin long dead, leaving his quest on Tarkir a failure
Ugin finally seemed to realize that a force had set him free, and became aware of Sorin back at the lip of the chasm.

claims.summary: In the rewritten timeline, Sorin finds Ugin alive and newly freed; in the original timeline he had found Ugin long dead.
claims.limitation: The quote does not say who or what freed Ugin, so this claim does not credit Sorin.

claims.subject: sarkhan_vol

evidence.quote: Ugin was alive, but dormant, locked away by Sarkhan's own actions.

claims.summary: Sarkhan's intervention in the past left Ugin alive but dormant (see A006/A028).

claims.subject: narset

evidence.quote: "Ugin," said Narset. "I need to speak to him."
But between you, me, and Ugin, there are three in this valley right now.

claims.summary: In the new timeline, the planeswalker Narset sets out to speak with Ugin, and Sarkhan counts all three as planeswalkers.
claims.limitation: The conversation itself is not shown in this source.

claims.subject: jace_beleren

evidence.quote: Jace was forced to undertake a dangerous journey to the Eye of Ugin, the center of the hedron network.

claims.summary: Jace travels to the Eye of Ugin to learn about the hedron network.

claims.subject: ugin

evidence.quote: Ugin, who was much older and much smarter than any of them, had given Jace two very clear directives: Don't try to kill the Eldrazi titans.
And don't let the titans escape to threaten other worlds.

claims.summary: Ugin told Jace not to kill the titans and not to let them escape.

claims.subject: ugin

evidence.quote: Ugin's missing allies, Sorin Markov and Nahiri the Lithomancer, still hadn't shown up

claims.summary: Sorin and Nahiri were absent when the titans fell, so Ugin's alliance did not reunite.

claims.subject: jace_beleren

evidence.quote: Jace closed his hands over the gleaming jewel suspended between Ugin's horns
for all the power he'd thieved from Ugin's gem

claims.summary: In Tarkir: Dragonstorm, Jace seizes the gem between Ugin's horns and draws on its power to command the Meditation Realm.

claims.subject: ugin

evidence.quote: as Ugin flung himself at his brother, trying to hold him in place, trying and failing

claims.summary: As Bolas broke free, Ugin threw himself at his brother and failed to hold him (see A009).

claims.subject: ugin

evidence.quote: Bolas and Ugin winking out of existence, eaten by the nothing, dead now, perhaps.
Narset had thought Bolas was dead and Ugin gone, but neither of these things proved true.

claims.summary: Narset sees Ugin and Bolas vanish; the same episode states both survived (consistent with A009/A010).
claims.limitation: This is Narset's point of view; 'dead now, perhaps' is her uncertainty, which the text itself then resolves.

claims.subject: elspeth_tirel

evidence.quote: "Narset, hurry—" Elspeth's voice, cutting through her horror of the future.
She felt mailed hands curl around her robes, lift her, carry her forward into the mouth of the Omenpath.

claims.summary: Elspeth calls to Narset, and armoured hands carry Narset into the Omenpath.
claims.limitation: The text names Elspeth's voice; that the 'mailed hands' are hers is inferred, not stated.

remaining: Targeted extraction: Chronicle of Bolas and the War of the Spark novel content are not covered here.
Kaya, Teyo and the Gatewatch's alliance with Ugin during War of the Spark need official web-story evidence; the cached War of the Spark side stories do not focus on Ugin.
No in-universe AR dates are asserted.
Card anchors and the Pilot 3 spec for build_lore_pilot.py are not yet written; any deck stays an UNAPPROVED proposal.
